In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L3 initial state is characterized by a combination of transfer from L1 and L2, and the upper limit of L3 attainment is characterized by convergence to the target language.
the advanced L3 English learners have converged on the L1 and L2 grammars of the relative clause.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
L1 transfer is the main source for the L3 initial state.
multilingual transfer models can predict L3 performance in the early stages of acquisition but that advanced L3 performance is not constrained by the L3 initial state.
the L3 English learners' knowledge of restrictive relatives is determined by L1 transfer in the initial stages and nativelike ultimate attainment in the advanced stages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the L3 initial stage and the advanced stages of L3 acquisition are not necessarily characterized by the same transfer patterns.
the L3 learners' L1 and L2 knowledge converge to form the L3 competence.
multilinguals' performance in the L3 is determined by the interaction of their L1 and L2.
